cards.label: h12_cache_hit
cards.text: Cache hit. A lookup succeeds because the desired record, requested block or matching key already resides in local cached storage. A read can return the saved value without contacting the original database or remote backing service.

cards.label: h12_cache_miss
anchors: retrieves the item from the data store
cards.text: Cache miss. The requested object is absent from cached memory; a failed lookup requires reading the authoritative backing store, fetching the missing value and possibly populating the cache.

cards.label: h12_write_through
cards.text: Write through. A cache update propagates synchronously to backing storage, with the write completed immediately at both layers rather than deferred to a later flush. Persistence is part of the write path.

cards.label: h12_write_back
cards.text: Write back or write behind. A modified value is initially held in memory, leaving dirty cached data. The application may finish before persistence; accumulated changes are flushed or synchronized to disk later by a background writer.

cards.label: h12_semaphore
cards.text: Counting semaphore. A finite resource pool is managed by a count of available permits or tokens. A participant acquires one before accessing the resource and releases it when finished; the count bounds simultaneous holders. Multiple holders may enter if permits remain.
